title: Velocity POC: weekly bench sync vs incumbent - AstraVantage
summary: Week 3 sync: reviewed end-to-end bench numbers comparing Redwood runtime vs incumbent. Redwood shows improved median latency and higher sustained throughput in most configs but there are tail spikes at high concurrency. Discussed quantization (int8), batching, KV cache warmup, and routing fallbacks. Agreed next steps to run targeted 95th percentile burst tests and share detailed CSVs and config recipe.
topics: Quantization and batch tuning (int8 vs fp16)
Pilot next steps and access to logs/traces
next_steps: Redwood to share tuned config and benchmark CSV by 2026-10-10
AstraVantage to provide access to sampler span/traces for two failing runs by 2026-10-12
Schedule deep dive on KV cache warmup pattern week of 2026-10-12
action_items: Maya Singh (Redwood) | Run 95th pct burst test with int8 quant + adaptive batching and share CSV | 2026-10-09
Carlos Mendes (AstraVantage) | Upload trace snippets for two high-tail incidents to shared dir | 2026-10-12
Jordan Park (Redwood AE) | Send updated SOW + pricing delta for dedicated slot option | 2026-10-11
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we have 54 minutes on the calendar, quick roll call?
[00:12] Carlos (AstraVantage): Carlos here, Priya and Liam joining from infra and platform. good to go.
[00:20] Jordan (Redwood): Great, Maya from our SE team is with me. we'll jump straight into the numbers, deck and live sheet are in the chat - bench link: https://redwood.link/bench-astravantage
[01:02] Maya (Redwood-SE): Quick note, these runs are seq len 128, sample gen 64 toks, we ran 3 seeds, warmup period 60s. incumbent is VendorX default endpoint in eu-west.
[02:10] Priya (AstraVantage): I saw the headline numbers but curious about P95 — we had a couple production blips previously at peak where latency doubled.
[02:35] Maya (Redwood-SE): Yes so median P50 for Redwood in the 8-concurrent test is 120ms per response (not per token), VendorX was ~240ms. Throughput sustained at 420 req/min vs 300 for incumbent at same concurrency.
[03:12] Liam (CTO): Those medians look great, but what about tail? we care a lot about 95/99.
[03:40] Maya (Redwood-SE): P95 is trickier — Redwood hit ~520ms P95 under the 32-concurrent stress, VendorX hit ~1.1s. But we saw 2-3 spike events that pushed it to ~1.9s, we think those align with cache misses and a full reload on one node.
[04:28] Carlos (Head of ML): Cache misses meaning KV cache or OS page cache?
[04:40] Maya (Redwood-SE): Primarily KV cache (prefix cache) — small percentage of requests were cold and incurred KV population overhead. Also one of the nodes saw a GC-like stall during the run (we have traces).
[05:05] Jordan (Redwood): We'll share trace snippets, one of Maya's runs shows the node-level recovery time.
[05:35] Priya (Infra): On the load generator side we were replaying live deviation patterns; some of the malformed prompts caused higher token counts — did you normalize for that?
[06:02] Maya (Redwood-SE): We normalized by clamping to seq128 for the bench, but you are right live variance can push seq length causing jitter. good flag.
[07:15] Jordan (Redwood): We also tried int8 quantization on a variant — results interesting. Maya?
[07:25] Maya (Redwood-SE): int8 reduced median by ~15-18% and improved throughput by about 22% in our runs. But quality regression for certain domain tokens was marginal — your team should validate against the eval set.
[08:02] Carlos (Head of ML): Any hallucination uptick with int8? we can't accept QA regressions for customer-facing flows.
[08:20] Maya (Redwood-SE): Not large in our synthetic eval, but we flagged a couple outliers. We can run A/B against your golden prompts.
[09:00] Liam (CTO): What's the packaging for dedicated? Preserving keys, KMS? we may want the dedicated pool for predictable tail behavior.
[09:18] Jordan (Redwood): Dedicated gives you reserved slots and avoids noisy neighbor effects; includes KMS integration for keys and optional on-prem control plane if you want. pricing delta TBD in SOW.
[10:05] Priya (Infra): if we go dedicated, what's the typical cold-start window for a model instance?
[10:18] Maya (Redwood-SE): Cold start for a new replica is about 20–40s for the model to fully load depending on quant and kernel path; we mitigate this with prewarm and standby capacity.
[11:03] Carlos: Back to bench numbers — did you test burst arrival (sharp ramp) vs constant rate?
[11:20] Maya: yes we did both. Under an 8x burst (ramp to 8x concurrency over 10s) Redwood's P95 increased to ~1.1s but recovered in 30–40s. VendorX took longer to recover and had more repeated long-tail events.
[12:05] Jordan: We put those burst CSVs in the sheet.
[12:30] Priya: We noticed a single run where memory footprint jumped — could be beam search variant?
[12:45] Maya: Might be tokenization or prompt template variance — we saw a different decoding path in that run, likely sampling params.
[13:20] Carlos: How sensitive are your batching gains to prompt length?
[13:32] Maya: Very — batching benefits are highest when sequence length is similar across requests. Variance reduces effective batch. We recommended prefix bucketing and a small dev-side preprocessor to normalize prompt lengths.
[14:40] Liam: Any repro we can run on our side quickly to validate? minimal script?
[14:50] Jordan: Yes we'll share a small harness and the exact config used (batch size, max tokens, kernel profile) — that'll be in the sheet.
[16:00] Maya: One more note: routing policy — we tested a fallback to a smaller quantized variant when GPU pressure hits 85% — that reduced error rates but added extra latency for fallback requests ~200ms.
[16:38] Priya: Hmm tradeoff. we prefer consistent latency over occasional lower cost.
[16:50] Maya: Understood. That's why dedicated with reserve is often recommended for production SLAs.
[17:30] Carlos: Bench vs baseline: at steady state Redwood is ~30–40% faster median and ~35–50% higher throughput depending on config. That's promising.
[18:05] Liam: Do you have cost delta estimates per 1M tokens between Redwood hosted and VendorX?
[18:20] Jordan: We're modeling cost both per-token and infrastructure cost. Early numbers show comparable token cost but lower infra/CPS due to batching and cache which reduces total TCO. We'll include an updated cost sheet.
[19:12] Maya: Also saw lower generation variance when we enabled prefix cache, but cache invalidation becomes a policy question if you have many dynamic prompts.
[19:50] Priya: For the failing runs we saw, can Redwood annotate traces with node id and event markers?
[20:05] Maya: yes, we can. Carlos if you upload the two capture logs we'll annotate.
[21:30] Jordan: Quick check: any blockers to the next week run?
[21:40] Carlos: no blockers, but we need the tuned int8 config and the harness.
[22:05] Jordan: we'll deliver those by Friday.
[25:00] Maya: Shipping plan: run a targeted 95th pct burst with int8 and adaptive batching; also run with dedicated slot sim to show tail improvements.
[26:12] Priya: How do you simulate dedicated slot locally?
[26:30] Maya: we restrict to a single pool node and pin model instance; that approximates reserved capacity.
[27:10] Liam: What telemetry will we need to expose so we can correlate the spikes?
[27:25] Maya: token-level latencies, model queue depth, KV hit/miss rates, and CPU/GPU util traces.
[28:40] Carlos: Are there any regulatory or data retention concerns with sharing traces?
[28:55] Jordan: We'll redact PII and you can host in your workspace; Redwood will sign the NDA terms already in place.
[30:00] Priya: Regarding security review, we need SAML SSO and RBAC details for engineers accessing logs.
[30:18] Jordan: our security packet covers SAML/SSO, SOC2, and key rotation practices — will resend.
[32:05] Maya: One technical ask — if you can surface a sample of prompts that caused long sequences we can run a tokenization pass to recommend bucketing rules.
[33:10] Carlos: we'll pull 50 anonymized prompts and upload.
[34:00] Jordan: any competitive motion from CloudGiant or OnPremOps we should be aware of?
[34:18] Liam: CloudGiant offered an integrated endpoint but the initial latencies looked worse in our quick tests. OnPremOps says their hardware gives lower latency but ops overhead high.
[35:00] Maya: Ok noted.
[36:30] Jordan: Recap — Redwood will: 1) share tuned config and harness (by 2026-10-09), 2) run and share int8 95th pct burst CSV (2026-10-09), 3) annotate traces once Astra uploads them (2026-10-12). Astra will: upload two trace snippets and 50 anonymized prompts (by 2026-10-12).
[38:10] Carlos: fine. also please include a short note about expected regression risk with int8 on our eval set.
[38:30] Maya: Will do, we'll run a small golden prompt A/B and report regressions.
[40:00] Priya: quick question on autoscaling — what are the cold-start mitigation knobs?
[40:15] Maya: prewarm replicas, standby capacity, and gradual scale up with queue shaping. We can tune thresholds to favor latency SLOs.
[41:50] Liam: any documentation links?
[42:00] Jordan: I'll drop the SRE playbook and the tuning guide in the chat.
[43:30] Carlos: last thing — what's the recommended guardrail for routing fallbacks? we don't want silent quality drops.
[43:50] Maya: set a maximum fallback rate and monitoring alert that bumps to canary if quality alerts cross threshold. We can ship a sample policy.
[46:00] Jordan: Thanks all — want to lock a deep dive next Tuesday for traces?
[46:10] Carlos: Tuesday works for us.
[46:40] Priya: we'll coordinate times.
[47:05] Jordan: I'll send the calendar and upload artifacts.
[48:30] Maya: Anything else on the bench numbers?
[48:45] Carlos: No, appreciate the granularity. Looking forward to the int8 runs.
[49:10] Jordan: Perfect. Closing notes: pushed updated sheet and links in chat.
[53:30] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and next steps. Bye.
